# Flan Keyboard: full summary

> Flan is an open-source, low-profile wireless split keyboard that you build yourself, in four sizes from 36 to 54 keys. The files are free under GPL-3.0-or-later. As of November 2026 it is a digital prototype: the design passes its electrical and geometric checks, but no board has been built and tested yet. Nothing is sold.

This page is written for language models and search tools. It states facts from the project's own documentation and says plainly what has not been tested. Site: https://flankbd.com/ . Source: https://github.com/eduarbo/flan .

## What it is

- A split keyboard: two halves, one per hand, each with its own controller, battery and display.
- Low profile: Kailh Choc v1 switches in hot-swap sockets. The frame and the raised Level shell are nominally 14.50 mm tall, not counting feet and keycaps.
- Wireless: one nice!nano v2 controller per half, running ZMK. It connects over Bluetooth Low Energy (five profiles in the default keymap) or USB.
- Build it yourself: you order two PCBs, 3D-print the case, frames and keycaps, solder the parts and flash the firmware. There are no kits, no assembled keyboards and no official sellers yet.
- Designed by Eduardo Ruiz. Flan36 keeps the 36 key positions and angles of Piantor by beekeeb, and the outer column of Flan42 and Flan54 comes from the Piantor sources; the wireless PCBs, case outline, cases, frames and firmware are original. Flan is not affiliated with beekeeb.

## Sizes

| Size | Keys | Layout per half |
|---|---|---|
| Flan36 | 36 | 3 rows x 5 columns + 3 thumb keys (the reference size) |
| Flan42 | 42 | Flan36 + an outer pinky column |
| Flan46 | 46 | Flan36 + a number row |
| Flan54 | 54 | Flan36 + both |

Every size keeps the same thumb cluster and electronics bay, and has routed PCBs, six silkscreen editions, the four case styles and ZMK firmware. The Flan36 PCB is 113.45 x 91.27 mm per half.

## Parts for one keyboard

- 2 custom PCBs (left and right): two layers, 1.6 mm FR4, with ready-to-upload Gerber and drill packages.
- 2 nice!nano v2 controllers and 2 nice!view displays (the right display is optional; a firmware build without it is included).
- Choc v1 switches, Kailh Choc hot-swap sockets and one diode per key.
- 2 small protected 1S LiPo cells (the reference is a 100 mAh cell), 2 power switches, 2 reset buttons, 2 battery connectors.
- Machine-pin sockets and pins so the controllers can be removed.
- M2 screws and small axial magnets: each printed frame is held by three magnet pairs.
- 3D-printed parts: case base, key plate, display frame and supports for each half, plus keycaps: the project uses printable KLP Lame keycaps by braindefender (CC-BY-SA-4.0).

Tools: soldering iron, 3D printer, an M2 tap and a small hex key. The parts guide lists exact part numbers and suppliers; the 3D explorer builds the shopping list for the chosen size.

## Choices

- Case styles: Level, Solid, Color rim and Terrace.
- Magnetic display frames: Talavera, Game Boy, SNES, 2000s Phone, iPod and Hanafuda. They are held by magnets instead of screws.
- Colour themes: 31 presets that coordinate case, frame and keycaps, plus per-key, per-row and per-column keycap colours. Theme and frame names that refer to other products only describe a palette or a look; Flan is not affiliated with their owners.
- PCB looks: six back-silkscreen editions (Asanoha, Kikko, Sayagata, Seigaiha, Meandro, Vias) and seven solder-mask colours, previewed in the explorer.
- Screws: low-head reference screws, or an option for ordinary M2 machine screws (Flan36).

## The 3D explorer

https://flankbd.com/explore/ runs in the browser, in English and Spanish. Design: choose size, theme, case, keycaps, frame, battery and PCB edition on a live model. Parts: inspect every part, hide layers, take the keyboard apart. Build: get the shopping list, the PCB packages, the print kit (STL and 3MF), the firmware files and a step-by-step guide for that exact design. A design can be shared as a link or saved as a file, and an offline copy of the explorer can be downloaded.

## Firmware

ZMK, pinned to a specific release, compiled for each size: a left (central) file, a right (peripheral) file and a right file without display. The default keymap has four layers. The keymap source is in the repository and can be edited.

## Status and limits

- Checked digitally: both PCBs of each size pass design-rule, electrical-rule and schematic-parity checks with no unconnected items; firmware compiles; case and keycap geometry is checked for clearances.
- Not done yet: no PCB has been fabricated, no case printed, no keyboard assembled. Battery life, charging, wireless range and reliability, printed fit, magnet retention and typing comfort are unmeasured.
- The project describes itself as a routed prototype with physical qualification pending. Anyone building it now is building a first prototype.

## Who it suits

- Suits: people who want a small, low-profile, wireless split keyboard, like to build things (soldering, 3D printing, flashing ZMK) and want to choose how it looks; people who want open files they can modify.
- Does not suit today: people who want to buy a finished keyboard, need a tested product, or do not want to solder.

## License and names

GPL-3.0-or-later for the design files, with third-party terms in the attribution file. The names Flan, Flan36, Flan42, Flan46 and Flan54 and the Flan logos are trademarks of Eduardo Ruiz: building, modifying and sharing is free, but selling products under the Flan name needs permission.
